title: HubSpot Reporting Dashboards for Small Teams — Jon Martin
seoTitle: HubSpot Reporting Dashboards for Small Teams
description: Databox, Geckoboard, and Klipfolio compared for small teams that report out of HubSpot: entry prices, trials, what each pulls from HubSpot, and who can view.
h1: Reporting dashboards for a small team that runs on HubSpot
dek: Three dashboard tools that sit on top of HubSpot, for teams that have outgrown the built-in reports or need to show numbers to people without a HubSpot login.
Prices and features below come from each vendor's own pages, checked on the date shown.

blocks.html: This page is for a small company, somewhere between a handful of people and a few dozen, that runs sales or marketing in {{link:hubspot}} and keeps getting asked for the same numbers. Someone exports a report every Monday, pastes it into a slide, and the numbers are stale by Wednesday.

HubSpot's own dashboards cover a lot. The tools below are for the cases they don't: blending HubSpot with ad spend or web analytics, showing numbers on a TV in the office, or sharing a live view with people who don't have a HubSpot seat.

Start with Geckoboard if the goal is a live screen for the sales or support team. Start with Klipfolio if you want the lowest entry price and unlimited users. Look at Databox if you need custom metrics across several sources, or across several HubSpot portals, and can carry its higher price.
Before you trial any of them, write down the five numbers people actually ask you for. A dashboard tool with a thousand connectors doesn't help if nobody agreed what a qualified lead is.

Databox prices its Platform plan at {{fact:databox.platform_annual}}, or {{fact:databox.platform_monthly}}. That plan covers {{fact:databox.platform_limits}}. There's {{fact:databox.trial}}. Agencies get a separate plan with {{fact:databox.agency_pack}}.
On HubSpot, Databox {{fact:databox.hubspot}}. That portal-merging piece is the reason an agency or a multi-brand company would pay Databox prices instead of a simpler tool.

Geckoboard's Essentials plan is priced {{fact:geckoboard.essentials_price}}, with {{fact:geckoboard.essentials_limits}}. Performance is priced {{fact:geckoboard.performance_price}}. You can try it {{fact:geckoboard.trial}}, and every plan includes {{fact:geckoboard.viewers}}.

Geckoboard's HubSpot integration covers {{fact:geckoboard.hubspot}}. Its HubSpot page also says you can {{fact:geckoboard.hubspot_no_upgrade}}. It is built for a live view on a screen, not for deep analysis.
Klipfolio's Base plan is {{fact:klipfolio.base_price}}, with {{fact:klipfolio.base_limits}}. Grow is {{fact:klipfolio.grow_price}}. The trial is {{fact:klipfolio.trial}}.

Klipfolio {{fact:klipfolio.hubspot}}. Per its HubSpot page, {{fact:klipfolio.hubspot_viewers}}. The four-hour refresh on Base is the trade for the price; it's fine for a weekly review and wrong for a sales floor screen.

If the question is what the team should look at all day, pick the tool built for a live screen. If the question is what leadership looks at once a week, refresh speed matters less than getting the definitions right.
If you manage more than one HubSpot portal, for clients or for separate brands, that narrows the field fast. Databox is the one of these three whose HubSpot page talks about merging portals.
Watch the limits that sit next to the price. Dashboards, editors, data sources, and refresh speed are where these plans differ, and the cheapest plan is usually cheap because of one of them.

Each of these tools connects to HubSpot through a login and an authorization screen. Whoever clicks through needs enough access in HubSpot to approve it, so sort out who that is before the trial clock starts.
Then clean the fields the dashboard will lean on: lifecycle stage, deal stage, owner, and source. A dashboard shows bad data faster. It doesn't fix it.

closing: Agree on the numbers first, then pick the tool that shows them to the people who need them at the speed they need them.

What it pulls from HubSpot.databox: HubSpot plus other sources, with custom metrics and portal merging.
What it pulls from HubSpot.klipfolio: HubSpot plus other sources, connected over OAuth.
